video_title: Micah Nori Media Availability | Oct. 9, 2026 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of unselfishness and ball security for the team
quotes.excerpt: taking care of the basketball is most important and then unselfishness, they kind of go hand in hand
quotes.quote: To me, taking care of the basketball is most important and then unselfishness, they kind of go hand in hand. I think you saw a little bit when you go back and watch the film from our first game is that they might have been a little bit too unselfish. If you have a layup and all that, I know we are all trying to integrate ourselves with our teammates, but shoot the ball. It is so much more fun to play with guys that are unselfish. No one has fun going and sitting in a corner and watching what is going on and not getting involved.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori wants the Blazers to be less unselfish on offense. He says players were passing up layups in the first game and notes that if you have a layup, shoot the ball.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Defining player roles and expectations for scoring and playmaking
quotes.excerpt: these guys are our primary ball handlers, these guys are our primary scores
quotes.quote: With our roles, we basically say these guys are our primary ball handlers, these guys are our primary scores. You still have to, if you see an open man, open jersey, pass it to them. But it will be clearly defined as far as who we want more so to look to score first if you will. And then also that will be said just in between how you set up your ATOs and running stuff for guys. But throughout the course of the game, we all want to throw ahead, look to score first, take the layups first, and then become playmakers after.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Blazers will have clearly defined roles for primary ball handlers and scorers, but emphasizes that players should look to score first and become playmakers after.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Denny's development and growth since joining the team
quotes.excerpt: Denny comes over here to Portland and he was in Washington, he didn't have the ball a lot
quotes.quote: Look at Denny, for example. In my opinion, Denny comes over here to Portland and he was in Washington, he didn't have the ball a lot in his hands. And then through injuries and through this and that, you stumble upon it and look what you find. So I think that is why I say you don't want to pigeonhole guys with their roles, but you definitely want to define what is expected of them.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Denny's growth since joining Portland: You do not want to pigeonhole guys with their roles, but you definitely want to define what is expected of them.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Hansen's potential as a playmaker and his role in the rotation
quotes.excerpt: Hansen is a big that we know is a very good passer that you can play through
quotes.quote: Hansen, for example, Hansen is a big that we know is a very good passer that you can play through, so you just want to situate that. And then when you see him do it, you are like, oh, here is a couple more things he can do. So that would be an example of it.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori highlights Hansen as a big man who can pass, noting that the coaching staff is finding new ways to utilize his playmaking ability.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: The team's luxury of depth and rotation flexibility
quotes.excerpt: we have the luxury of because with what we are going to do rotation wise
quotes.quote: I think that he has done a very good job and his showing has been very well. I think that is where we have the luxury of because with what we are going to do rotation wise and how we are going to play, if we are fully healthy, I don't know, it may be a spot here and there, maybe a couple bigs, Robert or Donovan get into foul trouble and those type of things and the matchup. So by any means, it is not like we are just counting Hansen out, but if there is an opportunity that arises, we feel very comfortable putting him in the basketball game.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Blazers have the luxury of depth and will rely on situational rotations, but confirms they feel very comfortable putting Hansen in the game when opportunities arise.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Identifying leadership qualities in players like Tumani
quotes.excerpt: everybody that is capable of leading you want to lead
quotes.quote: Everybody that is capable of leading you want to lead. And I think when I said that Tumani is a leader, he is. But he is more comfortable just leading in practice and leading one-on-one than having to be the voice of the team. But to your point, what Tumani has done is you can kind of see, I don't think that leaders you can force people to lead. And I think that if people are willing to follow them and they are all about the right things, those are what leaders are.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Tumani's leadership style: He is more comfortable leading in practice and one-on-one than being the voice of the team, but he leads by doing the right things.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Tumani's defensive impact and non-verbal leadership
quotes.excerpt: Tumani, you watch the way he goes about his business defensively on the floor
quotes.quote: Tumani, you watch the way he goes about his business defensively on the floor, everything that he is doing, guys are kind of want to gravitate towards him and he is more than willing to help. He is a communicator. So that is why I say I mentioned him because he is leading these guys. And a lot of his stuff can be leading non-verbally just with how he plays defense. And again, if you don't compete at a high level defensively when the Drew Holidays and the Tumanis and Robert and those guys are all on the floor and Donovan, you are going to stick out like a sore thumb.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praises Tumani's defensive impact, noting that his non-verbal leadership and high-level defensive effort set a standard that forces the rest of the team to compete.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Tumani's defensive analytics and high-level consistency
quotes.excerpt: he was in the 100th percentile of his matchup every single night
quotes.quote: He is a guy that you love to have on your team. He doesn't need the ball. A lot of guys that defended at his level, basically, I think he guarded, if you look at the analytics, he literally had, he was in the 100th percentile of his matchup every single night, meaning he guarded better offensive players than anybody in the league night in and night out. And he is not one of those guys that all of a sudden if he doesn't get a touch four minutes into the game is going to be like, I am not guarding. He doesn't pout. I mean, we have to make sure that we do get him involved. It is kind of like the defense tags, the rebounding tags that you have to play. But what I love about him is Tumani is the same guy every single day, high character, smile on his face, loves to compete, loves to play basketball, cares about his teammates and is going to go and do about the right things.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Tumani was in the 100th percentile of defensive matchups last season, guarding the best offensive players night in and night out without ever pouting about his offensive touches.
